title: $52.88m returned by the US in 2025
simple: In 2025 the US agreed to return $52.88 million in assets linked to a former petroleum minister. $50 million was set aside for electricity in rural areas, managed by the World Bank. The rest went to a rule-of-law institute. We have not yet found a public report of how the $50 million has been spent.

verdict.text: $50 million set aside for rural electricity, managed by the World Bank
How the $50 million has been spent: no public report found yet
$2.88 million set aside for a rule-of-law institute (IIJ)

summary: On 10 January 2025 Nigeria and the United States signed an agreement to return about $52.88 million from the forfeited "Galactica" assets, which are linked to former petroleum minister Diezani Alison-Madueke and her associates. She has denied wrongdoing. About $50 million was to fund rural electrification through the World Bank, and $2.88 million was given as a grant to the International Institute for Justice and the Rule of Law (IIJ). Officials said the World Bank and IIJ would send regular reports to Nigeria and the US.
gaps: We have not yet found a public report from the World Bank or the government on how the $50 million has been spent, or which communities got electricity.
We have not yet found a public report on how IIJ used its $2.88 million.

timeline.text: The US Justice Department files a civil case to recover about $144 million in assets. It alleges they were bought with bribes paid to the former minister, who has denied wrongdoing.
Nigeria and the US sign an agreement to return $52.88 million: $50 million for rural electricity through the World Bank, and $2.88 million for IIJ.

nodes.label: United States (forfeited "Galactica" assets)
nodes.simple: The US recovered these assets through a court case and agreed to give the money to Nigeria.
nodes.description: The assets are linked to former petroleum minister Diezani Alison-Madueke and her associates. The US case began in 2017 as a civil forfeiture complaint. She has denied wrongdoing. The return agreement was signed in Abuja on 10 January 2025.

nodes.simple: $2.88 million was set aside as a grant for a rule-of-law and counter-terrorism project.
